title: Graceful epochal switchover with circuit quarantining for active-active gateway
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: In active-active hosted API rollouts we see two classes of instability during region failovers: (1) abrupt traffic shifts cause transient p99 spikes and KV cache misses that break streaming session continuity; (2) noisy-region error bursts cascade into global retries and saturate healthy regions. Goal: Implement an epochal switchover protocol that (a) performs observable, time-boxed traffic attenuation per region, (b) fences/quotarines regions that trigger circuit thresholds to limit blast radius, and (c) preserves streaming session continuity wherever possible via session fencing tokens and KV cache pre-warm handshakes. Success metrics: reduce cross-region p99 latency spikes during failover by >=45%, limit error amplification events to <1/month, and preserve >=95% of active streaming sessions without manual intervention during planned and unplanned region handovers.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled attenuation: weighted routing can perform a 10-step linearly decreasing traffic shift over 5 minutes with telemetry at each step
Circuit quarantine: a region exceeding 5% 5m error-rate while p99 latency>2s triggers automated quarantine that prevents >10% additional traffic routing to that region
Session continuity: streaming sessions using session-fence token can resume in target region within 8s end-to-end without client reauthentication for >=95% of sessions
Observability: dashboard shows per-epoch metrics (step latency, queue depth, KV miss rate) and can correlate to rollback/onwards decisions
Chaos-tested: end-to-end integration test simulating KV-store lag, partial instance loss, and ingress partition demonstrates graceful attenuation with no more than 5% increased token cost vs baseline
design_decisions: Use epoch numbers attached to session tokens: each switch operation increments an epoch; requests carry epoch to allow thin gate logic at edge to determine if session needs handoff
Progressive attenuation vs instant cutover: selected linear multi-step attenuation (default 10 steps over configurable window) to give KV and cache layers time to warm in target region
Circuit quarantining: adopt a two-tier breaker — soft breaker for automated weighted reduction (backoff) and hard quarantine which removes routing weight until auto-heal or manual unblock
Telemetry signals: primary signals are p99 latency, 1m error-rate, request backlog depth, and KV miss-rate; combined into a small hazard score to avoid noisy single-signal triggers

Streaming handoff: implement a short-lived resume token (epoch + session id + checksum) that allows receiver-side rehydration of stream state from a synchronized KV snapshot; we accept a trade-off of additional KV replication traffic for continuity
implementation_notes: Edge changes: implement epoch header parsing and soft/hard breaker logic in gateway routing layer; add per-connection drain hooks for streaming sockets
KV sync: extend existing KV checkpoint API to support quick delta snapshot for session resumes; optimistic RPO acceptable for 5s window
Control plane: add 'epoch' concept to rollout controller and expose step control in Console Rollouts UI with manual override
Autoscaler interaction: ensure attenuation does not trigger aggressive scale-to-zero; expose expected qps per-step to Dedicated autoscaler
Testing: unit tests for epoch collision, integration tests for resume token flow, and staged canary in us-west-2 to validate metrics and dashboards
